Alvarez will face WBC super middleweight champion Christian Mbilli in Saudi Arabia in Alvarez's first fight since September 2025.In Alvarez's previous fight, he suffered the most humbling defeat of his professional career, dropping a clear decision to Terence Crawford. Crawford was the much better fighter that night, using his world-class skills to beat Alvarez to the punch and constantly disrupt his rhythm.Unlike Alvarez's prior losses, he was not the far more inexperienced fighter facing a hall of famer (like against Floyd Mayweather Jr.) or the smaller man coming up in weight against a pound-for-pound elite (as was the case against Dmitry Bivol). Alvarez was younger than Crawford with a history of huge fights and Crawford was moving up multiple weight classes for the mega-payday of facing Canelo.Be sure to keep up with all the action on Saturday with our live coverage of Alvarez vs. Mbilli, including round-by-round scoring and updated fight results throughout the night!
What happened against Crawford seemed to validate all the doubts that had built up over the years. Alvarez has a ton of in-ring miles on his body at 36 and has seemed to have lost a few steps in recent years. Plus, Alvarez has not scored a stoppage since 2021. Time seemed to be catching up to Alvarez, and against a fighter as skilled as Crawford, there was no escape for the then-undisputed champion.

"After 20 years as a professional, I'm glad to be here," Alvarez said I'm the challenger now, but always in my mind, I'm the champion. Tune in on Saturday, because it's going to be a special night."I don't believe in shortcuts. I'm going straight for the champion because I already have the experience. I've been a champion for many years and I want to be a champion again."
Those doubts, and the question of how much Alvarez has left in the tank, lead us to Saturday and Mbilli, who was promoted from interim to full champion when Crawford retired following his win over Alvarez.Mbilli is a hard-charging fighter who has yet to taste defeat in his professional career, putting up a 29-0-1 pro record with 24 knockouts.Mbilli won the WBC interim belt with a first-round knockout of Maciej Sulecki, the second first-round knockout in a three-fight span for Mbilli. His first defense of the interim belt came against Lester Martínez on the undercard of Alvarez's fight with Crawford.
Against Martinez, Mbilli was on his usual game early, coming forward, throwing big right hands and working the body, but he fatigued down the stretch, which has been a recurring problem for the muscular Mbilli. The result of the fight was a very competitive draw that could have realistically gone either direction."My training camp was perfect. My mind is ready for this fight," Mbilli said. "I don't need to do anything special to win; I only need to be myself. That's how I'm going to win this fight." Let's take a closer look at the rest of the fight card on Saturday with the latest odds from DraftKings before getting to a prediction and expert pick on the main event below.

Add to those problems that Mbilli has only been scheduled for a 12-round fight once (his first-round knockout win over Sulecki), and you can see the areas that Alvarez has clear advantages.The biggest question for the fight is what Alvarez has left in the tank. title: Jeremiah Smith's Heisman hopes take hit after Ohio State's offense sputtered in USC loss - CBS Sports
description: Luke Fahey's debut in L.A. didn't go as planned and the Buckeyes' star receiver may slide out of the Heisman favo
body:
Luke Fahey's debut in L.A. didn't go as planned and the Buckeyes' star receiver may slide out of the Heisman favorite status
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 31, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:59 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        No one was quite sure what to expect from the Ohio State offense coming out of a bye with a new quarterback under center after Julian Sayin's potential season-ending injury late in the win over Indiana two weeks ago. A 30-18 loss on the road at USC was a concerning one for the Buckeyes on a number of fronts. The obvious is that this is a team with national championship aspirations, and while Fahey wasn't disastrous, the Buckeyes struggled to create big plays against a Trojans defense that has been among the Big Ten's worst this season at limiting explosives. A secondary concern in Columbus, though one that resonates nationally, is Jeremiah Smith's Heisman campaign. Smith entered the week as the solid favorite ahead of Miami's duo of Darian Mensah and Malachi Toney, but after Saturday's loss in L.A., he slipped to third in the odds (+340) behind both of the Hurricanes' stars at FanDuel Sportsbook. Smith had a productive game against USC with 10 catches (on 12 targets) for 83 yards and one touchdown, and the target share suggests he'll still have a puncher's chance to hold onto the Heisman he seemingly got one hand on in the first half of the season. The concern is that USC's defense was figured to be one of the friendliest Ohio State would get to play down the stretch, and Smith put up a relatively pedestrian game by his standards this season -- with much of his production coming late, with Ohio State trailing by three scores. 
That's a missed opportunity for Smith, and with Oregon, Northwestern, Nebraska, and Michigan left on the schedule, one wonders if he will have a chance to finish with the flourish he needs to hear his name called at the Heisman Trophy ceremony in early December. Can Luke Fahey give Smith a chance for big plays? Fahey went 21-of-38 for 260 yards and one touchdown, but his accuracy down the field left an awful lot to be desired -- as did his efforts when the Buckeyes got into the red zone. Much of his work was done in the short-to-intermediate passing game, asking Ohio State's skill players to make plays. That's understandable -- and rainy conditions in L.A. certainly could have exacerbated issues throwing downfield -- but considering Smith came into the game averaging just under 19 yards per catch, a game with 8.3 yards per reception is a considerable decline. When Fahey did try to push the ball downfield, he was typically well off target, including a miss on what should've been a long Smith touchdown, where he had two steps on his defender but slipped while trying to adjust to a ball that was well underthrown. 
USC came into the game having given up 11 passes of 30 yards or more (83rd in the country), but Smith's long on the night was 27 yards. Each of their next four opponents is statistically better defensively at preventing explosive pass plays, and while Fahey was eager to target Smith, most of those came in the short and intermediate zones. Early in the season, Smith's Heisman campaign and Ohio State's offensive goals were aligned. Sayin throwing down the field to Smith was their primary objective, but with Fahey they seem likely to shift to a more run-heavy approach when able -- trailing big against USC helped skew the run-pass balance considerably -- and to try to keep Fahey comfortable in the passing game, with less emphasis on throwing deep. Smith's Miami problemIf that is indeed the approach Ohio State takes, the biggest problem for Smith is that solid performances won't be enough. If Fahey isn't able to connect on the few deep shots he attempts, it's going to be incredibly difficult to put together the kinds of games that will keep him in the conversation with Mensah and Toney. 
Miami is headed in the opposite direction in terms of game flow, as a leaky Hurricanes defense means Miami has to let it rip with their star quarterback-receiver combo all game. That duo was strong against UNC in a shootout win in Chapel Hill on Saturday, with Mensah taking over favorite status (+170) after a 22-for-29 passing performance for 274 yards and three touchdowns. Toney (+290) only had seven catches for 75 yards, but did haul in a pair of those touchdowns, including the game-sealing score in the final minutes. With Notre Dame up next week for Miami, it's the Hurricanes stars that will get the spotlight performance and a chance to create a late Heisman moment in a huge national TV spot. Smith's chances at this point feel to be as much in Notre Dame's defense's hands as anything, as he needs the Irish to stymie Miami's star duo to give himself a chance at ending his sensational Ohio State career with the nation's most prestigious individual award. Smith is going to exit Columbus as the best receiver in Big Ten history. He has a case as one of the best college football has seen in recent memory, but if he's going to join the exclusive list of receivers to win the Heisman Trophy, it's going to require him winning what's becoming an uphill battle. 
Smith is going to need his young quarterback to show rapid improvement, get a little help from the Canes (and the Irish), and create some spectacular after-the-catch plays with fewer downfield opportunities. That's all possible, but for the first time all season, he's slipped out of favorite status for the Heisman, and both he and the Buckeyes have to have some concerns about their quarterback situation moving forward.

title: Lincoln Riley flips script on hot-seat chatter as USC's upset over Ohio State puts Trojans back in CFP picture - CBS Sports
description: The biggest win of Riley's USC tenure came at home against the second-ranked Buckeyes on Saturday night
body:
The biggest win of Riley's USC tenure came at home against the second-ranked Buckeyes on Saturday night
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 31, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:18 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Back against the wall and facing music reaching scream-metal decibels about his job security, Lincoln Riley delivered.For only the sixth time in 21 tries at USC, the Trojans toppled a ranked opponent under Riley, and it was a big one Saturday night against second-ranked Ohio State.USC's 30-18 victory pushes Riley's squad back in the College Football Playoff discussion as part of the group that controls their own destiny entering the season's final month — with an outside shot at a Big Ten Championship Game appearance, too.Poetically, this was his middle finger to questions surrounding his future and failure to meet expectations in Los Angeles. The Trojans still have elite opportunities remaining against Indiana — a one-loss team that's leaking oil with quarterback issues — and unbeaten UCLA during rivalry weekend.
Riley was 1-6 all-time against AP top-six opponents coming in, that lone victory coming in the form of a 31-16 decision over the Buckeyes in just his second game as a head coach back at Oklahoma in 2017."If I didn't want to be at this place, I wouldn't have come here in the first place," Riley said this week before the biggest win of his USC tenure. "I've had plenty of opportunities to leave. This is where I want to be. This is the right place for me. I'm the right person to be here. And that's as honest and transparent as I can be with you guys."I love it here. I mean, like I told you guys a lot of times, there's not many people in college football history that gave up what I gave up to come here. I don't care if it's 15 years down the line; that never should be taken lightly. It's certainly not taken lightly by me. I came here because I believe in this place and none of that has changed whatsoever."
USC put together a solid plan defensively to combat Heisman frontrunner Jeremiah Smith, limiting him to 83 yards receiving and a touchdown on 10 catches. Ohio State freshman quarterback Luke Fahey, who was making his first career start in place of injured Julian Sayin, never found a rhythm in the passing game and was chased out of the pocket throughout.Trojans quarterback Jayden Maiava registered 222 yards through the air and a score, while running backs King Miller and Waymond Jordan combined for 126 yards and two touchdowns on the ground.The loss for Ryan Day was only his sixth in 65 games against Big Ten competition with the Buckeyes.
USC's path to CFP berth, Big Ten Championship GameNow 7-2 overall and 4-2 in conference play, the Trojans find themselves in a three-way tie for third in the conference standings after Week 9. With Indiana, Maryland and UCLA left, winning out gives USC three victories this season over ranked teams and puts the Trojans in prime position for an at-large CFP berth for the first time in program history.To play in Indianapolis with a Big Ten title on the line, however, scenarios are a bit less clear:USC wins out and ...UCLA loses to Minnesota, Illinois or MichiganNorthwestern loses to Iowa, Ohio State, Minnesota or IllinoisWisconsin loses to Rutgers, Maryland, Purdue or MinnesotaOregon loses to Ohio State, Michigan, Michigan State or WashingtonOhio State loses to Northwestern, Nebraska or Michigan  Nebraska loses to Washington, Illinois, Rutgers, Ohio State or IowaIllinois loses to Nebraska, UCLA, Iowa or Northwestern (since it owns a common opponent win over Oregon)Iowa loses to Northwestern, Purdue, Illinois or Nebraska  (since it owns a common opponent win over Wisconsin)Essentially, the best USC can finish is 7-2 in Big Ten play and needs tiebreakers over five different teams — UCLA, Ohio State, Indiana, Northwestern and Nebraska — should those finish with the same record.

A potential playoff appearance, considering hard-to-stomach losses this fall against Oregon and Wisconsin, would make this campaign a raging success regardless of how the Big Ten standings shake out.

title: Georgia escaped Florida, but passing-game concerns threaten title hopes - CBS Sports
description: Georgia's defense and ground game have masked issues through the air, but tougher opponents could force the Bulld
body:
Georgia's defense and ground game have masked issues through the air, but tougher opponents could force the Bulldogs to open things up
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 31, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:57 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Coming out of its bye week, No. 3 Georgia began its home stretch with a big 27-8 win over No. 17 Florida. You never snub your nose at a three-score rivalry win, but the Bulldogs' offensive performance wasn't as rosy as the scoreboard might suggest.Georgia totaled just 318 yards of offense against a Florida defense that has been leaky all season, but, to be fair, some of that was due to the defense. The Bulldogs forced four turnovers. One of them resulted in a scoop-and-score, and two more resulted in short fields, which Georgia converted into 10 points.The biggest question about the Dawgs' offense after this win is the passing game. The running game eventually found some consistency, allowing Georgia to lean on the Gators in the second half. Quarterback Gunner Stockton, on the other hand, couldn't find much success against one of the worst secondaries in the conference.Entering the game, Florida ranked 13th in the SEC and 121st nationally in passing yards allowed per game (255.0). The Gators also ranked 112th in EPA per dropback (0.23) and 126th in passing success rate (50.7%).
Despite that, Stockton finished the game with just 101 passing yards on 13-of-23 passing. Freshman Craig Dandridge was the team's leading receiver with 39 yards, and 32 of those yards came on the Bulldogs' longest pass play of the game.In his postgame interview with ESPN's Holly Rowe, Kirby Smart complimented Stockton's grit and willingness to run the ball but admitted that Georgia has to get better through the air."We missed some throws," Smart said. "We left some points out there. We gotta get better."
He's not wrong. If Georgia wants to achieve its goal of winning the national championship, Stockton and his pass-catchers will have to be much better than they were today, and that day may come sooner rather than later.Big tests coming for BulldogsOver the next three weeks, Georgia will face quarterbacks capable of scoring points, even against one of the best defenses in the conference.Trinidad Chambliss and Ole Miss are stepping into the batter's box, Austin Simmons and Missouri are on deck, and LaNorris Sellers and South Carolina are in the hole.
There's a good chance at least one of those quarterbacks forces Georgia to engage in a higher-scoring game. If that happens, are the Bulldogs capable of answering the bell?Stockton has turned in some big games this season. He threw for 295 yards and three touchdowns against Vanderbilt, and he made some incredibly difficult throws in Georgia's road win over Alabama. Still, the lack of production against Florida is a red flag.For starters, even when some of the production is there, Stockton has been prone to mistakes. Just look at the Bulldogs' loss to Auburn. He played well for 90% of the game, but his three turnovers played a key role in the Tigers leaving Athens with a win.
It doesn't help that Georgia hasn't had any playmakers emerge in the receiving game. Dandrige is the team's leading receiver with 20 receptions for 349 yards. The Bulldogs are loaded at tight end, but none of those players have become real threats in the passing game on a consistent basis. Lawson Luckie leads that group with 12 catches for 197 yards and two touchdowns.Maybe the Bulldogs can get through the regular season by patching together their passing attack. After all, the defense is capable of holding talented quarterbacks in check. We've already seen that with Keelon Russell. Who's to say that unit can't give Chambliss, Simmons and Sellers problems too?But Georgia's ultimate goal isn't to go 11-1 in the regular season. It isn't even to win the SEC Championship. The Bulldogs have their sights set on a national championship, and they will likely encounter potent offenses along the way. Miami, Notre Dame, and LSU are all capable of putting crooked numbers on the scoreboard. Ohio State has the best player in the country, with Jeremiah Smith putting up monster numbers every week.
At some point, Georgia will need its passing attack to make big plays, and it's fair to wonder whether that will happen when the moment arrives.

title: Tomorrow's Top 25 Today projects college football rankings after Week 9 - CBS Sports
description: A chaotic Week 9 creates major shake-ups across the AP poll as Miami holds onto No. 1, Georgia climbs and open sp
body:
A chaotic Week 9 creates major shake-ups across the AP poll as Miami holds onto No. 1, Georgia climbs and open spots invite plenty of new arrivals
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 31, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:53 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            8 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Though the Week 9 schedule did not set up a handful of ranked-on-ranked games, the results of another chaotic week in college football have led to more than a handful of top 25 teams taking losses. The shake-ups will prompt some big changes in the college football rankings, none more impactful than USC's win over Ohio State in Los Angeles. USC was previously unranked after falling from the AP Top 25 poll after a 17-7 loss to Wisconsin. The Trojans endured immense pressure all week after the defeat, feeling the weight of an offense that was underperforming and the threat of an opponent in Ohio State that was arriving with a top-two ranking. USC answered its offensive questions immediately and raced out to an early lead, riding that momentum to a rain-soaked signature win for Lincoln Riley. It marked his first-ever win against a top-five opponent as USC's coach, and it will launch the Trojans back into the top 25. As for Ohio State, it is predicted to be among the lucky ones who lost in Week 9 but won't fall too far, thanks to wins against the likes of Indiana and Iowa in conference play. But with teams like SMU, Northwestern, Arizona, Oklahoma State and Wisconsin all taking losses on Saturday, the door is open for plenty of new arrivals in the rankings. Here's how we expect the new AP Top 25 to look on Sunday after Week 9:  1. Miami (Last week — 1): Even though the No. 1 team in the country was trailing in the second half, the upset alert always seemed a little premature as long as Malachi Toney was on the field. Miami's Heisman Trophy-contending wide receiver was absolutely electric in the Hurricanes' 38-35 win, finishing with seven catches for 75 yards and two touchdowns. 
2. Georgia (3): The Bulldogs cashed in on Florida's early mistakes for easy points and rode another strong performance from the defense to a sixth straight win in the Cocktail Party rivalry. At 7-1 overall with a convincing win against a quality team, Georgia may pick up a couple first-place votes, but the overall rating will be left unchanged for most voters. 3. Notre Dame (5): It took a minute for Notre Dame to hit its stride, but the voters are not going to be quick to overreact one way or another to a 35-13 win against Navy. All eyes are on next week's showdown with Miami, where a firmer judgment of the Fighting Irish as a top-five team can be made. 4. Utah (6): On a week where a couple of top teams got off to slow starts, credit Utah for sending a message early against Cincinnati. The Utes raced out to a 42-6 halftime lead and then cruised in the second half as attention turns to next Saturday's showdown with BYU. The fact that the Bearcats just upset Texas Tech set up for a potential letdown spot but also allowed for Utah's dominance to validate an 8-0 record that's going to get more respect from the voters.  
5. UCLA (7): Voters are not going to rush to any major adjustments in where the Bruins stand after beating Nevada 27-0. The shutout win, highlighted by four defensive takeaways, keeps the best piece of UCLA's ranking resume intact, and that's the zero in the loss column. UCLA is now 8-0 overall, but its best win remains the victory against three-loss Oregon earlier this month. 6. Indiana (4): Last week the Hoosiers held just a one-point advantage on Notre Dame (1,459 to 1,458) and an edge of less than 50 points compared to Utah. After another overtime win that was light on offensive production and heavy on upset scare, Indiana could be poised to give up a couple spots to those other teams who were also battling for top-five positioning. Indiana's resume does not hold up well upon intense scrutiny, with Nebraska and Northwestern as the best wins and mostly a "quality loss" argument thanks to the four-point defeat to Ohio State.  7. BYU (8): It seemed as though the Cougars were cruising with a dominant defensive performance early and a 17-3 halftime advantage, but a second-half charge from Arizona State had BYU sweating a little bit at the end of a 27-20 win. Ultimately, the win, by any margin, should keep the Cougars solidly ahead of Kentucky and Alabama, both of whom were off in Week 9.  
8. Kentucky (9): The Wildcats were off in Week 9 and will be back in action next week at Tennessee. 9. Alabama (10): The Crimson Tide were off in Week 9 and will be back in action next week at LSU. 10. Texas (11): We are not anticipating too much change after the Longhorns took advantage of a Kamario Taylor-less Mississippi State team and cruised to a 31-3 win to improve to 6-2.  
11. Ohio State (2): The drop for Ohio State in the rankings will hit on two fronts. First, Saturday night's loss came to a USC team that was previously unranked and changes the analysis for the Buckeyes, as they are now a two-loss team. But the other aspect here is that Week 9 was the first time we got to see Ohio State play four quarters without injured quarterback Julian Sayin, and the offensive production numbers reflect a group that isn't operating at the same level that it was previously. That will impact voters looking to slot Ohio State among other top teams, and make it more likely they choose the Texas head-to-head result as an anchor for the Buckeyes' new ranking position.   12. Ole Miss (12): Playing at home in a lookahead spot with Georgia coming to town next week, it would have been easy for Ole Miss to get caught in a dogfight with an Auburn team that clearly can throw punches with SEC heavyweights. So credit the Rebels for handling business in a 45-17 victory. 13. Texas Tech (13): There is an argument that Texas Tech's resume got noticeably better with a win against Arizona, but we also are not expecting voters to overreact to a one-score home win as a top-15 team. Though significant for the establishment of a new Thomas Castellanos-led offense, the win keeps the Red Raiders mostly around the same spot in the rankings.   
14. Wake Forest (14): Among the many highlights for Wake Forest in a 51-7 romp of Virginia was another outstanding day for Carlos Hernandez. The Demon Deacons wide receiver had eight catches on nine targets for 136 yards and a touchdown, marking the fourth time he's hit 100 yards in a game this season. Wake Forest is now 7-1 overall and will face FCS Merrimack next week before heading to SMU with a chance to play its way into the ACC Championship Game in November.    15. LSU (15): The Tigers were off in Week 9 and will be back in action next week against Alabama in Baton Rouge. 16. Tennessee (16): The Vols were off in Week 9 and will be back in action next week against Kentucky.  
17. USC (NR): Lincoln Riley believes in this team and has now guided the Trojans back into the thick of the Big Ten title race with a key head-to-head win against Ohio State. Now the challenge for the Trojans will be to close the deal with more big-time wins as they will be on the College Football Playoff Selection Committee's radar and likely ranked in Tuesday's first CFP Rankings. 18. Houston (18): The Cougars were off in Week 9 and will be back in action next week against Cincinnati.   19. Boise State (20): An injury to Maddux Madsen clouds an impressive response to Texas State's upset effort, as the Broncos held on for a 46-45 win behind backup quarterback Max Cutforth. Madsen was seen on crutches after the win, which now has Boise State at 7-1 overall with an in-road to Pac-12 title contention.  
20. Missouri (23): Ahmad Hardy returned to the lineup, and Missouri returned to its winning ways with a 34-10 rivalry win at Arkansas to improve the Tigers to 6-2 on the season. It's been 21 days since the last Missouri win, so voters should feel better about having Eli Drinkwitz's group as a top 25 team, and that ranked status sets up for a very interesting showdown with Texas back in Columbia next weekend. 21. Iowa (NR): Last week's balloting had Iowa finishing 26th in voting points and closer to No. 25 Wisconsin than Wisconsin was to No. 24 Oklahoma State. A thorough dismantling of the Badgers will prompt a bump up into the top 25, taking some of those Wisconsin votes along with a level of respect for the dominant nature of the victory. 22. South Carolina (NR): It's seemed like three seasons in one for South Carolina, who now has built a three-game winning streak with victories against Florida, Tennessee and Oklahoma after a three-game losing streak that had the hot seat conversation roaring. The Gamecocks smashed the Sooners on Saturday, cruising to a 42-25 win in Norman behind another stellar performance from LaNorris Sellers. 
23. New Mexico (NR): The Lobos had already popped up on several ballots last week, and now at 7-1 could stand out as a more attractive option compared to some teams on the cut line with multiple losses. 24. Oregon (NR): The Ducks carry a chaotic collection of wins and losses, boasting victories against both USC and Northwestern but also being weighed down by a trio of defeats to UCLA, Oklahoma State and Illinois. Beating the Wildcats in Week 9 could prompt a bounce back into the rankings as three-loss teams get more consideration, and given some of the other upheaval, the door is open for Oregon to sit among the top three-loss teams in the country. 25. Florida (17): The woeful offensive performance from the Gators could result in a quick bounce from the top 25 even as the Gators do have some of the best wins in the country. The reasons to keep Florida ranked are the high-end wins against Ole Miss and Texas, but in current form, this team has lost three of its last four and currently looks stuck in the mud offensively. 
Projected to drop out: No. 19 SMU, No. 20 Northwestern, No. 22 Arizona, No. 24 Oklahoma State, No. 25 Wisconsin

title: Borussia Dortmund spoil Harry Kane's Ballon d'Or coronation, keep pace in Bundesliga title race - CBS Sports
description: Fabio Silva scored in the dying minutes of the game to ensure Dortmund would come out with a 2-2 draw at Bayern M
body:
Fabio Silva scored in the dying minutes of the game to ensure Dortmund would come out with a 2-2 draw at Bayern Munich
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 31, 2026
                            
                    at
    7:10 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        MUNICH – Few things are as straightforward as handing the ball to a Ballon d'Or-winning striker from the penalty spot. So when Harry Kane stepped up in the 56th minute at the Allianz Arena, there was little reason to expect anything other than a goal on a day that seemed tailor-made for him. Before kickoff, Bayern Munich had turned Der Klassiker into a celebration of Kane's Ballon d'Or triumph. Accompanied by his family, Kane walked onto the pitch carrying the trophy as Bayern unveiled a giant banner bearing his likeness in the center circle and flag-bearers waved red-and-white Bayern flags around the pitch. The striker even wore a special red jersey with gold trim befitting the game's newest golden boy. Yet five days after collecting soccer's most prestigious individual award, Kane drove his penalty against the crossbar, the ball ricocheting back into play rather than over the line.The miss was not a deterrent for Bayern, who went on to unleash 23 shots worth 4.05 expected goals to Borussia Dortmund's 12 and 0.63. The numbers reflected their status as the Bundesliga's undeniable heavyweight, pinning Dortmund back for long stretches as the Allianz Arena swelled with every attack and groaned with every near miss. For once, though, life came at Bayern fast. Kane's penalty was merely the first sign that this would not be a routine Der Klassiker. A 2-2 draw followed, ensuring the title race would survive another weekend and leaving the two sides level on points, just as they had entered the night.
By the numbers, Bayern had done enough to win and may have left feeling aggrieved by the crossbar's intervention. It denied Kane from the spot and, deep into stoppage time, thwarted Lennart Karl's curling effort from the edge of the box. Yet the hosts never fully established the relentless rhythm that has become their hallmark. Bayern generated chances in waves, but Dortmund repeatedly found moments to slow the tempo, relieve pressure and remind their rivals that control of the match was never quite as complete as control of the shot chart. The match ebbed and flowed, each team enjoying meaningful stretches of possession, creating a tension that lingered until the final whistle.To Dortmund's credit, they identified the only realistic way to blunt Bayern's superiority. The visitors did not stop Bayern from attacking, a near-impossible task these days. Instead, they prevented the match from becoming the avalanche Bayern so often creates. The hosts managed 15 touches in Dortmund's penalty area through the opening 37 minutes, a figure consistent with their season norms, but they needed more time and more passes to get there. Dortmund shared possession almost evenly for the first half hour, slowing Bayern's tempo and holding them to 284 touches in that span, well below their Bundesliga average of 344.9.The quality of Bayern's chances lacked their usual verve until Konrad Laimer's 38th-minute strike turbocharged an attack that has rarely missed a beat, even without Luis Diaz (hamstring). Kane's penalty proved to be the match's inflection point, though, a moment that revealed the competing realities at the heart of the draw. Bayern saw a match they largely controlled but failed to put away. Dortmund saw proof that resilience, rather than dominance, might be enough to keep pace.
"I probably could have been out there for another hour today and the ball wouldn't have gone in the back of the net," Kane said afterward. "You have to take that on the chin sometimes ... It's nothing to cry about."Kane's response reflected Bayern's outlook. They left frustrated but hardly concerned, armed with enough evidence to believe the performance mattered more than the scoreline.For Dortmund, the miss felt like a reprieve. Der Klassiker has often become an exercise in surviving Bayern's pressure, and for a moment it looked as though the visitors were about to confront a two-goal deficit. Instead, Kane's effort rattled the crossbar and gave Dortmund belief -- something that was increasingly valuable as the match wore on.
"Harry is such a great penalty taker," Dortmund goalkeeper Gregor Kobel said. "You can't really predict it, but I just tried to [not] give him anything. The last time I tried to fake him out a little bit, but then the timing for me was a little bit bad in the last game. Today, I thought I'd just give him nothing. I tried to make it hard as soon as possible for him and luckily it worked."
Belief, not control, became Dortmund's currency. Bayern continued to create chances and monopolize threatening territory, but the visitors gradually turned the match into the sort of uneven, uncomfortable contest they needed.Serhou Guirassy was a likely candidate for Dortmund's equalizer, while Dayot Upamecano joined Laimer on Bayern's scoresheet in the 66th minute. For another 22 minutes, it felt like the hosts were inching closer to their preferred outcome -- Kane and Michael Olise may not have been the clear standouts on Saturday, but Bayern's squad is constructed well enough that other players can handle the slack. If the night was supposed to belong to Kane, it ultimately created room for an unlikely headliner. That role fell to Dortmund's Fabio Silva.
The Portuguese forward is not among the first names on Dortmund's team sheet, but he is steadily developing a reputation as one of Niko Kovac's most dependable options. His goal against Bayern was his fourth in all competitions this season, already eclipsing last season's total despite spending much of the campaign in a reserve role. Though his goals have attracted attention, Silva's seven assists last season serve as a reminder that his value extends well beyond finishing chances."Every game is important for me," he said. "It's not about scoring against Bayern. I'm just thinking of helping the team with my football. Not all about goals. I remember two or three actions before the goal, I was there to help the team to create some chances. I think I'm as a player more than [just about] scor[ing] goals … Of course, I prefer [to] start than be on the bench. If I say the opposite, I'm not going to be 100% honest with you, but I always try to be positive during the week when I see I don't play. Of course, the first moment I'm angry, but after, I try to always be positive because I know I can be important for the team."Dortmund will continue to face questions about whether they can truly match Bayern over the course of the season. Saturday night did little to erase them. The shot totals, expected goals and overall flow of the game all pointed toward Bayern's superiority. Yet title races are not decided by underlying numbers alone. On a day built to celebrate Kane's coronation, Dortmund left Munich with something nearly as valuable -- proof that Bayern can be frustrated, and that the race remains alive.

title: Thomas Castellanos' performance in win over Arizona raises ceiling for Texas Tech - CBS Sports
description: Joey McGuire's bold switch at quarterback unlocked a dormant rushing attack, giving the Red Raiders a dual-threat
body:
Joey McGuire's bold switch at quarterback unlocked a dormant rushing attack, giving the Red Raiders a dual-threat dimension that re-establishes them as Big 12 title contenders
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 31, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:38 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        In the waning moments of No. 13 Texas Tech's game against No. 22 Arizona, the Red Raiders faced a critical opportunity to put the game away. First-time starting quarterback Thomas Castellanos took a carry for only a few yards on second down, pulling down the linebackers and setting up third-and-one. The Red Raiders lined up in a two-back set, seemingly setting up another quarterback run. Castellanos set the ball in the mesh point for a read while the defense collapsed. Instead of pulling, running back J'Koby Williams clutched the ball, took one cut right and broke off a dramatic 64-yard run to put the finishing touches on a dramatic 34-26 win to wrestle control of the Big 12 back. Texas Tech coach Joey McGuire made a bold move, benching quarterback Will Hammond in favor of the journeyman Castellanos. But after finding their offense in the second half, Castellanos unlocks a new ceiling for the Red Raiders heading into the home stretch. 
Castellanos was a late addition to the Texas Tech roster after receiving an injunction, primarily rostered to give the Red Raiders some experienced depth behind first-year starting quarterback Will Hammond. But several weeks into Hammond's starting tenure, results were poor. Despite playing a relatively light schedule, the Red Raiders ranked bottom half in the Big 12 in total offense under Hammond's watch. The running game, especially, was lackluster as defenses stacked the box and challenged an inconsistent offensive line. Hammond threw six touchdowns to six interceptions in his starts. While Castellanos is less of a factor in the passing game, the threat of his rushing is a game-changer for the Red Raiders. Seven of his carries went for first downs, and he broke off a pair of carries for 20-yard gains. Castellanos became the first Texas Tech quarterback to record 100 yards rushing since Tyler Shough. 
Castellanos threw for 144 yards and two touchdowns and added 117 yards and a score on the ground. But beyond the rushing production, defenses are forced to account for all 11 players. The switch made a huge difference for running back J'Koby Williams, who exploded for 175 yards and a touchdown in the win. The 328 yards rushing was the most surrendered by an Arizona defense since 2020, a 0-5 pandemic season under Kevin Sumlin. Since a 28-17 loss to BYU, the Wildcats have been on a tear. They won their last three games by an average of 28.0 points per game and rattled off a five-game winning streak. It was a prime opportunity for the Wildcats to knock off the reigning champs, coming off of a frustrating loss. Instead, Arizona gave up 34 points, the most since Sept. 27, 2025, against No. 14 Iowa State. 
To be clear, Castellanos has plenty of his own issues. The senior completed only 5 of 15 passes in the first half and 11 of 24 for the game, even below his career average of 58.5% completion. His passing is primarily a wrinkle on a run-based offense. Furthermore, Castellanos is still playing on a temporary injunction. Earlier this season, Castellanos briefly lost eligibility after a previous injunction was dissolved. Texas Tech can't be 100% confident that their new quarterback will stay eligible through the end of the season. Despite the drawbacks, Castellanos gives Texas Tech a much-needed spark heading into the home stretch of the season. With the 30-game starter in the lineup, the Red Raiders seriously re-enter the Big 12 race.

title: Steelers vs. Browns: Rivals battle in Week 8 with first place in AFC North on the line - CBS Sports
description: Plus, where to watch, what to know and a preview from an NFL expert
body:
Plus, where to watch, what to know and a preview from an NFL expert
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 31, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:06 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        One of the NFL's greatest rivalries is alive and well. On Sunday, the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cleveland Browns will duel with first place in the AFC North on the line. Both teams enter Sunday's game with 5-2 records. The Browns, by virtue of their Week 4 win over Pittsburgh, are technically the division leader. Cleveland responded to a loss to the Jets in Week 5 with wins over Baltimore and Tennessee. Pittsburgh has won three straight since losing to Cleveland. Last Sunday, the Steelers became the first team to win a game in Paris after recording a 16-10 win over the Saints. Here's how you can follow the action, along with a breakdown and a prediction. Where to watch Steelers vs. Browns liveWhen: Sunday, Nov. 1 | Time: 1 p.m. ETWhere: Acrisure Stadium -- Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania TV: CBS | Stream: Paramount+ Follow:  CBS Sports AppOdds: Steelers -3.5, O/U 39.5 (via DraftKings Sportsbook)Steelers vs. Browns: Need to know Last time we met: The Browns' 27-24 win over Pittsburgh in Week 4 was their fifth consecutive win over the Steelers in Cleveland. The Browns led 21-7 before withstanding Pittsburgh's comeback attempt. The Steelers' comeback was spearheaded by Aaron Rodgers, who threw two fourth-quarter touchdown passes. 
The Steelers tied the score with 1:42 left, but four completions by Deshaun Watson on Cleveland's ensuing drive set up Andre Szmyt's game-winning 56-yard field goal with 10 seconds remaining. Rodgers threw for 299 yards with three touchdowns and two interceptions in a losing effort. Jaylen Warren ran for 93 yards on 17 carries, and DK Metcalf led Pittsburgh's receivers with 115 yards on five catches. Cleveland's offense ran through rookie receivers Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion, who combined to catch nine passes for 153 yards. 
Steelers are finding their groove on both sides of the ball: Pittsburgh's three-game winning streak is largely the byproduct of better play from the offensive line and a defense that is continuously improving. Pittsburgh's offensive line surrendered five sacks of Rodgers back in Week 4. Rodgers has been sacked nine times in the three games since. While that's still not great, it is a sign of the unit's continuous improvement.The line has also helped revive the Steelers' rushing attack, which has improved further with Rico Dowdle's return. The duo specifically made their presence felt during Pittsburgh's game-winning drive in overtime in Tampa Bay back in Week 6. 
Defensively, the Steelers have made marked improvements since the loss in Cleveland, which was the Steelers' first game after Joey Porter Jr. was traded to Dallas. The unit is currently fifth in the NFL in points allowed, fourth in touchdown passes allowed, sixth in average yards per carry allowed, seventh in third-down efficiency and eighth in red zone efficiency. Linebacker Payton Wilson has been one of the Steelers' defensive standouts during the winning streak. He made a key interception during last week's win over the Saints. Browns offense ready to take off? While Cleveland's defense has been solid all year, its offense has at times left something to be desired. They are coming off their best performance in recent moments, however. 
Against the Titans, the Browns piled up 491 yards while receiving excellent balance. They threw for 308 yards and ran for 183. Cleveland did turn the ball over twice after not doing so a week earlier in a 13-10 win over the Ravens. Really, the big question in Cleveland is whether or not Watson can beat an elite defense. He'll try to show that he can on Sunday. Prediction The Steelers have two distinct advantages. They have the better quarterback and a running game that should be able to take advantage of a Browns defense that is 22nd in the NFL in average yards-per-carry allowed. If Dowdle and Warren get going, that should help open things up for Rodgers and the passing game. Score: Steelers 20, Browns 16

title: College football winners, losers: Dylan Raiola bounces back, Wisconsin falls flat - CBS Sports
description: Indiana escapes on a miracle field goal and Wisconsin gets blanked by Iowa as the early slate delivers chaos acro
body:
Indiana escapes on a miracle field goal and Wisconsin gets blanked by Iowa as the early slate delivers chaos across the top 25
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 1, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:44 am ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Week 9 college football slate looked like a lighter one, but there are always surprises to be found. Seven AP Top 25 teams dropped in the first two windows of the day, including five to unranked opponents. No. 2 Ohio State dropped to USC in the most stunning performance of the day, losing Ryan Day's second career game against an unranked opponent. No. 1 Miami was also pushed, but ultimately survived. Of course, No. 3 Georgia continues to flex its muscles, eviscerating rival Florida. No. 4 Indiana, though, needed some late heroics from its kicker. No. 13 Texas Tech finally looked the part of a Big 12 contender, while No. 25 Wisconsin's season slid to a screeching halt. Here are the biggest winners and losers of Week 9.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Loser: Ohio StateNo. 2 Ohio State's loss to USC came with a freshman quarterback in the lineup, but there was an awful lot that felt off about it. The Buckeyes were bullied in the secondary, including giving up a 69-yard touchdown on the second play of the game. The offensive line struggled to get consistent push. USC scored on four of its first six drives, with another ending on a fumble in Ohio State territory. 
Aside from a late loss to Texas, Ohio State has managed to hold on to games by the skin of their teeth, including a tight battle against a flawed Indiana team. Now, the Buckeyes are proving that they're mortal. Ohio State had not lost two games before November since 2011. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: Iowa StateThe Cyclones went through one of the most dramatic roster transformations of the offseason after losing nearly their entire two-deep to Penn State. Now, Iowa State is putting itself in an unlikely position for a bowl game after stunning No. 24 Oklahoma State 51-49 on a game-winning field goal. After a few tough weeks against elite competition, running back Aiden Flora broke out again with 221 yards and two touchdowns in the win, including a 75-yard breakaway touchdown. The Cyclones never blinked when potential No. 1 pick Drew Mestemaker kept dropping bombs, and now, they play four straight games against unranked opponents to close the year. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Loser: NebraskaOnly days after announcing a new contract with quarterback Anthony Colandrea that will keep him in Lincoln through 2027, the Cornhuskers lost a brutal game against Washington. The Cornhuskers led 7-3 until the game's final 90 seconds, when the Huskies threw a touchdown pass to take their first lead. With a chance to either tie or win the game, Colandrea stepped back and threw an awful decision to safety Alex McLaughlin, who returned the pass 48 yards for a game-sealing touchdown, only 15 seconds of clock later. Nebraska has now lost three games straight by a combined 13 points. The curse of the Huskers lives on. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: RB Ahmad Hardy, MissouriCollege football got a real scare over the summer when All-American running back Ahmad Hardy suffered a gunshot wound during a concert. There were real concerns about Hardy's future career and life, especially as doctors opted to leave the bullet lodged in his leg because of the danger of removing it. Against all odds, Hardy returned to the field against Arkansas on Saturday. He recorded only three carries in his return, but broke off a dramatic 37-yard run in the fourth quarter. While Missouri will benefit from the return of one of college football's best running backs, his story will inspire fans across the sport. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: Indiana coach Curt CignettiHow does he keep getting away with it? No. 4 Indiana was dead to rights after Minnesota drilled a 60-yard field goal in the waning seconds of regulation. Cignetti appeared to completely mismanage the clock, letting 40 seconds run instead of taking a timeout. 
Then, Indiana miraculously nailed a 60-yard field goal of their own and produced the game-winning play to open overtime in a 23-16 victory against the Golden Gophers. Indiana is clearly diminished from its national title team, but it doesn't matter. Cignetti just, somehow, manages to find a way. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Loser: WisconsinThe vibes were exceedingly positive in Madison after an impressive few performances to get Wisconsin back into the AP Top 25 under coach Luke Fickell. All the goodwill was spent in an instant as the Badgers lost a 30-0 stunner against Iowa. Wisconsin was completely outclassed on both sides of the ball, mustering only 52 yards rushing. They allowed Iowa quarterback Hank Brown to complete 20-of-24 passes for 222 yards and two touchdowns, one of the best quarterback performances in years for the Hawkeyes. 
All the momentum from a breakout 2026 season is gone for the Badgers. Closing the year out with four unranked victories to reach nine wins would be nice, but below the expectations of this team after last week's domination of No. 16 USC. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: Texas TechObituaries were started for Texas Tech's season after a stunning two-touchdown loss to Cincinnati last week. Instead of panicking, coach Joey McGuire handed the keys to backup quarterback Thomas Castellanos. The Red Raiders have now outdueled No. 22 Houston and No. 22 Arizona in impressive home performances, launching them into the Big 12 title discussion. With road trips to No. 24 Oklahoma State and Baylor remaining, the Red Raiders have a few more prove-it spots against two of the hottest teams in the conference. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: QB Dylan Raiola, OregonThe Raiola era at Oregon has been a mess ever since he was forced into the starting lineup in place of Dante Moore. After going down 10-0 against No. 20 Northwestern, it looked like the Ducks were heading towards another disastrous performance. After the early adversity, Raiola rose to the occasion. The Nebraska transfer completed 22-of-31 passes for 336 yards and three touchdowns in one of the best games of his career. New offensive coordinator Jay Johnson did a much better job of letting Oregon's star-studded receivers make moves in space. Oregon's playoff hopes are likely doomed, but a road trip against No. 2 Ohio State next week makes things awfully interesting. It's a major spot for Raiola to cement himself as a repaired prospect. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Loser: OklahomaThe Sooners just keep finding new lows as Brent Venables heads towards his third losing season in five years. This time, it was a stunning 42-25 loss to South Carolina at home in a game that likely spelled the end of offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle. For the first time this season, the Sooners' defense completely collapsed. The Sooners allowed 28 points in the first half alone and looked outmatched. There were multiple coverage busts, including an 84-yard breakaway for a touchdown from LaNorris Sellers to DJ Black. At this point, Oklahoma under Venables is bad at everything. The Sooners scored 15 points in garbage time to make the score look respectable, but this was a collapse. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: QB DJ Lagway, BaylorFor the second year in a row, DJ Lagway saw his coach fired. But under interim Baylor coach Joe Klanderman, Lagway played perhaps the best game of his career. Facing one of the stingiest defenses in the Big 12 in UCF, Lagway set back and picked them apart. He threw for 319 yards and four touchdowns without an interception, completing 64% of his passes in a 41-9 victory. It could just be a simple dead cat bounce, but Baylor played with more urgency than it has seen in years. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Loser: SMUWith only one close loss on their record, No. 19 SMU looked like a potential spoiler in the College Football Playoff race. The Mustangs were a solid No. 3, within striking distance of Wake Forest and Miami. But after a stunning 30-27 loss against Syracuse, it's another frustrating season of what-ifs. 
The Mustangs have been painfully close the past several years to returning to the College Football Playoff, including a loss to California on the last play of the game. This was similarly painful, giving up a passing touchdown with 17 seconds remaining to a team that entered at 3-4 and searching for any consistency. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Winner: Sacramento StateThe Hornets had a brutal transition to FBS, losing their first seven FBS games by an average of 27.5 points per game. But finally, against Kent State, the Hornets recorded their first-ever FBS victory, 31-10. Running back Isaiah Ene rushed for 107 yards and two touchdowns in the win, and the Hornets can build some confidence as the season heads into the home stretch.

title: NFL Week 8 final injury report: Patriots' AJ Brown ruled out, latest on Lamar Jackson, more - CBS Sports
description: A rundown of each team's final Week 8 injury report
body:
A rundown of each team's final Week 8 injury report
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 31, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:22 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Injuries are becoming a greater factor as the NFL's regular season nears its midway point. Some teams continue to be hit hard by the injury bug, while others have been relatively lucky in avoiding too many serious injuries. The Ravens are among the teams that have already dealt with a notable injury to a star player. The good news for Baltimore fans is that Lamar Jackson will play this week after an ankle injury sidelined him for the past three games. The Ravens need all the help they can get as they prepare to face the Bills and MVP front-runner Josh Allen. Below is a rundown of each team's final Week 8 injury report. Keep tabs on this page as we'll be providing updates throughout the evening. Ravens at BillsRavens: S Jaylinn Hawkins (knee), G Vega Ioane (knee) OUT; RB Adam Randall (neck), CB T.J. Tampa Jr. (knee) QUESTIONABLE Bills: WR Tyrell Shavers (knee) OUT; OT Spencer Brown (back), CB Dee Alford (ankle), TE Dalton Kincaid (chest), WR DJ Moore (shoulder), DT Greg Gaines (lower body)
Randall and Tampa were recently designated to return to practice from injured reserve. Both players were full participants in practice on Thursday and Friday. For the Bills, Kincaid wore a non-contact jersey during Friday's practice, but that didn't stop him from drop-kicking a tackling dummy after making a catch.         No. 3 Georgia and No. 17 Florida will be squaring off somewhere other than Jacksonville for the first time since 1995 on Saturday, as the historic rivals take the World's Largest Outdoor Cocktail Party indoors at Atlanta's Mercedes-Benz Stadium on Saturday. With Jacksonville's EverBank Stadium under renovation until August 2028, the setting will be different.The stakes remain the same. In fact, there may be an even higher degree of intensity to this year's showdown between the border foes because of the circumstances. It's the first time since 2020 that both are ranked in the top 20 of the AP poll. Georgia (6-1, 4-1 SEC) is coming off a bye week after a stunning home loss to Auburn, and Florida (5-2, 3-2) is riding high off an Oct. 17 road win over Texas. First-year Gators coach Jon Sumrall already has two wins over top-10 teams (Ole Miss and Texas) and could get his team firmly in the College Football Playoff hunt with another marquee win.The Bulldogs have won five straight meetings in the series, but Sumrall has reinvigorated the Florida program this season since arriving from Tulane. The Gators have shown the ability to slay some of the SEC's top dogs already this season, and Georgia will need to be on high alert to avoid suffering consecutive regular season losses for the first time since Kirby Smart's first season in 2015.
Where to watch Georgia vs. Florida liveDate: Saturday, Oct. 31 | Time: 3:30 p.m. ETLocation: Mercedes-Benz Stadium -- Atlanta, GeorgiaTV: ESPN | Live stream: Fubo (try free)  Georgia vs. Florida: Need to know  Florida's quarterback situation: Starting in place of the injured Aaron Philo, Florida sophomore Tramell Jones Jr. rose to the occasion in a Week 7 win at Texas. The inexperienced quarterback completed 22 of 35 passes for 155 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions against the Longhorns' vaunted defense while also totaling 41 rushing yards. But will he play against Georgia? Philo was listed as questionable on the Gators' first student-athlete availability report this week, raising questions over who will get the nod under center. Florida coach Jon Sumrall said Monday that he doesn't plan to name a starter before the game, which will force Georgia to prepare for both QBs. Jones is more mobile, but he's also put his full repertoire on tape now. Philo is still dealing with a right shoulder injury, but he did practice this week.Georgia's run defense: Regardless of who starts at quarterback for Florida, the Gators are going to try and lean on their run game. Georgia's run defense has shown some vulnerability in the past two games. Led by quarterback Byrum Brown, Auburn totaled 192 yards rushing against the Bulldogs in an Oct. 17 upset road win over UGA. The week before, Alabama amassed 161 yards on the ground against Georgia. Up until those two games, Georgia's run defense had been stout. Facing Florida might be the toughest test yet of Georgia's ability to stop the run. The Gators raced to a 4-0 start, including wins over Auburn and Ole Miss, by rushing for 200+ yards in each game. The UF rushing game has been less effective in three games since then, but star back Jadan Baugh is a load to handle. He leads the SEC in rushing touchdowns with 13 and is third in rushing yards with 763.
CFP implications: Georgia's chances of reaching the College Football Playoff will rise to 94.5% with a win, according to the CBS Sports CFP Forecaster. Those odds would dip to 72.7% with a loss. Entering Saturday, Florida has just a 9.5% chance to make it, but that mark would surge to 29% with an upset win over the Bulldogs. On the flip side, suffering a third loss would leave UF with just a 5.6% chance of making the playoff. If the Gators suffer a third loss against Georgia, they would need to run the table against Oklahoma, Kentucky, Vanderbilt and Florida State and then get some help from other teams to have any shot at reaching the field with a 9-3 record.Georgia vs. Florida prediction, picksExpect to see an angry Georgia team after the Bulldogs were forced to stew on a turnover-fueled home loss to Auburn during a bye week. Florida will have the Bulldogs' full attention after an upset win at Texas, and UGA won't be remotely caught off guard by anything the Gators attempt offensively. Georgia's defensive staff knows Florida offensive coordinator Buster Faulkner well. On the opposite side, the Gators have shown they are vulnerable on defense, and Bulldogs quarterback Gunner Stockton will be playing with a chip on his shoulder after a rare poor performance against Auburn. Pick: Georgia -12.5

        The 2026-27 college basketball season begins Sunday when Villanova faces Notre Dame at Palazzo dello Sport in Rome, Italy. The season is starting a day earlier than usual after the NCAA granted special clearance for the teams to face each other in a monumental showdown. This matchup has been months in the making, with CBS Sports' Matt Norlander the first to report on it earlier this calendar year. The NCAA quietly approved a waiver in January to allow the teams a one-day head start, given the historic precedent of the matchup. Immediately following the men's game, Notre Dame's women's team will face Villanova. 
        
            
                Holy hoops! Villanova, Notre Dame finalizing plans to open 2026-27 college basketball season in Rome, Italy
                
                    Matt Norlander                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Notre Dame and Villanova are both prominent private Catholic schools with connections to Pope Leo XIV. Robert Francis Prevost is a 1977 alumnus of Villanova, and Notre Dame is regarded as the world's most prominent Catholic institution of higher learning. Notre Dame even has an outpost in Rome. While this matchup is historic on the men's side, it isn't unprecedented on the women's side. Duke opened last season against Baylor in Paris. This season, No. 1 South Carolina will face No. 20 Maryland on Nov. 2 at Adidas Arena in Paris. In 2023, South Carolina opened the season against Notre Dame at Halle Georges Carpentier Arena in Paris. 
With the season on the horizon, here is everything you need to know ahead of Villanova's matchup with Notre Dame on Sunday.  Villanova vs. Notre Dame: Need to know 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    A first for everything: The matchup between Villanova and Notre Dame is believed to be the first men's season opener on foreign soil and the first regular-season Division I basketball game in Italy. This matchup has been quite literally months in the making, with plans announced for this game nearly 10 months ago. This game will be played at Palazzetto dello Sport, which seats approximately 3,500 people for basketball and has been around since the 1950s. It remains unclear whether the Pope will attend the game: The Palazzetto dello Sport, the venue for the historic matchup, is located approximately 30 minutes from the Pope's residence in Vatican City. The Pope held a private audience on Saturday with all four teams and their traveling fans. Approximately 7,000 people are expected in the Paul VI audience hall inside the Vatican. 
New era for Notre Dame: The Fighting Irish were among the teams hit the hardest by the transfer portal earlier this offseason. Notre Dame's three leading scorers from last season (Markus Burton, Jalen Haralson and Cole Certa) all departed the program. With plenty of new faces and Notre Dame being on the verge of its longest NCAA Tournament drought since the 1990s, the pressure is on coach Micah Shrewsberry heading into Year 4 of his tenure. A win against a strong Villanova squad that won 24 games last season would be a great place to start.
